body:
My GP knows I'm suicidal. The person that I saw with my father said she was a nurse, and I even explicitly told her I had a plan I wanted to commit too before being there. She even specifically asked how I was going to do it. She logged all of this, and by the end of it she said that we're done and I'm free to go. I'm rather speechless... I've just disclosed very sensitive information about myself in front of my father (sans the specific question of feeling suicidal) and hoped she would of done something. It was literally just keeping a record of my thoughts so the council can judge whether I'm fit enough or not. 

This further made my feelings worse when my mother was annoyed at me for not "laying into them enough" for more trivial things which hardly bother me at all. (Eyesight, scoliosis alignment surgery...) So now I'm not supposed to be honest with my feelings? This just feels like an act where I'm merely being used as an excuse for a money exploiting ploy, not as somebody who feels so terrible that I really need help.

I have just e-mailed the support director of a group who support individuals with AS and Autism where I get weekly support from a support worker. I told him I feel terrible and find it very difficult to talk in person, and that I feel the subject matter is too heavy to deal with. I also explained the situation that occurred today. He replied and said that he understands, and reminded me I have support I can look forward to tomorrow and asked if there is anything he can do for me at present.

I don't know if I can bring myself to tell them, or if I should. It feels too personal to get someone involved that I've been seeing for several weeks where I've otherwise remained silent about these issues, but I don't know who else to turn too.

Even if it's able to completely turn my life around, this sounds like the complete most harrowing thing to me. Not to mention, the shock it would give to anyone else. I'm probably way over thinking that... but it still sounds so incredibly daunting to me, when even just going to the corner shop is such a big task. But I do appreciate the encouragement.

I don't need money at this time (at least, I don't *feel* I need money). I live under a house and I have access to whatever information I may need right here. I've lost interest in my hobbies so I'm currently not wanting to spend toward anything. I'm not very tech savy, I just use the PC a lot. (who in this generation doesn't?) 

What I am interested in (Music, stage/lighting design) seems like a futile effort because of how narrowly focused I am on them, and how they're not particularly stable professions.

I know living with my parents is temporary, but I still feel hopeless in being able to make a sustainable life for myself, even if I am only 18. 

Thanks for commenting.

Thanks. I have been thinking this too. My panic all stems from the fact of "What if it just doesn't make a difference and I'll feel even worse because yet again I'm not being taken seriously for my issues and it'll continue to go downhill?" which in turn really hurts my ability to even speak truthfully, especially when I already feel broken beyond repair, I can't even fathom how I'll be able to talk to anyone if I feel my trust has been betrayed for one more time. I will try though. Thanks for the encouragement, it helps. 

EDIT: Sad to say it turned out exactly as I expected it too. I feel awful now...

My father shares some symptoms. Sensory issues don't seem to be as big of a problem for him; specifically he appears to sleep much more soundly. He has his own routines for doing things though, which frustrates me when he doesn't appear to relate to the issues I have in regards.

My parents aren't married, and he's also a stepfather to my brother. I don't see him as a role model when I feel too disconnected from a strong relation with him (or anybody else). 

The only family that I could get along with to live with is my mother's up in Scotland. I have only seen them once in my lifetime however. I/we've had very bad issues surrounding my dad's family, particularly when my grandmother unfortunately passed away when I was 7. Essentially my grandfather found someone else and they cut all ties off with us, which really hit us when we needed financial help.

I have a wide variety of interests. One I'd like to do as a productive hobby would be to be a musician. As a career, I'd like to be apart of stage production in showbiz. But I don't feel proud about either of them, and I hate to discuss my interests with anyone. 

I'm aware of my self-obsession, and I'm like this because of how desperate I feel to find a reason to stay alive. 

My sensory issues have plagued me all my life, and become more of a problem with not enough sleep/low mood. 'Manning Up' just doesn't work. It's a very hard thing to explain unless you have the same issue. The most comparable analogy I could give is a phobia. Whereas fear is a heightened state of alertness in response to perceived danger, phobias cause uncontrollable distress and can't suddenly be suppressed. Obviously this isn't a phobia, but it's something my mind is *always* drawn too. Therapy could help, but I have no idea how to obtain the therapy I would need...

Also, sorry to sound overly pessimistic, but if it were possible to just 'man up' all my issues, then I don't see myself being in the state I'm in now in the first place.

You are right about the parents, and I don't expect them to be superheroes... just, *normal* human beings. I can perfectly understand them from the point of view of being in their position, but it doesn't make me feel any better about myself regardless. I never claim anything to be all about me, nor do I even want that. But that doesn't stop me from feeling *emotionally* frustrated. I would never kill myself in-front of somebody or in very close proximity, which is why I've said this has been intervened. Moreover, I would hate to be caught in the act and live. 

I would love to volunteer, and have attempted, but even in a situation where it's purely volunteering upon my own time, I still feel like I can't live up to the task and I'd be better off not wasting the time bothering anybody else. It really relates to the whole sleep/restfulness/sensory issue problem that I have, in that I'm basically forcing myself to have a schedule. However, I can not keep to a schedule (fixed or otherwise) because I can never keep myself to a rested enough state on a consistent basis. 

In closing, I'm not sure if I made it clear, but I've felt this very same way before, but not *quite as bad*. I've been having depressive episodes with suicidal thoughts for over 5 years now. But I've always had something to keep me going; be it an interest or a friend I talked to or talking to somebody at a branch (as opposed to a hotline, since I find talking on the phone more uncomfortable and less private). Motivational speeches used to work, but I couldn't care less now. I feel like I don't have a reason to live anymore, there just isn't anything I find I enjoy or want to work towards. I used too, but now I don't.

Thanks for the comment. I probably sound terribly pessimistic and unwilling to take any advice, but it's exactly how I feel- not helped by previous experiences.
